function.name: dft_open_structure
function.description: Open a structure file from this chat, by its name, in DFT Workbench, the embedded goldilocks-core panel -- required before dft_review, dft_download_bundle or dft_magnetic_orderings can be called. Parses and validates the structure; no DFT parameters are chosen yet. Returns a summary of the structure (partially occupied sites must be ordered before goldilocks-core recommends anything), the calculation it opened into (code, task, HPC profile and overrides, kept from the previous structure except the structure-specific overrides listed in cleared_overrides), and the tasks goldilocks-core offers.

file_name.description: The exact name of a structure file in this chat: a file the user attached (the NAME in '[Attached file: NAME]') or the filename a get_structure call returned. DFT Workbench reads the file itself, so never pass the file's content.

function.name: dft_settings
function.description: List the settings DFT Workbench can change for the current calculation, as its panel shows them: the code, task and HPC profile with their options, then every parameter setting (functional, pseudopotentials, cutoffs, k-points, smearing, magnetism, job resources, ...) with its key, type, options, unit, current value and the source that decided it, and whether the user set it. Read-only. Call it to find the key for a setting before dft_set, or to show the user the options.

group.description: Only this group's settings, e.g. 'k_sampling', 'occupations' or 'job'. Omit for all.

function.name: dft_set
function.description: Change settings in DFT Workbench, exactly as the user would in its panel: the task (e.g. band structure, phonons, a relaxation), code, HPC profile, and any parameter setting. Only set values the user gave or named, never values of your own; if the user wants a change without saying the value, show the options from dft_settings and ask. If their goal fits several tasks without naming one, ask which. Keys are goldilocks-core's own (dft_settings lists them); null puts a setting back to automatic. All values are checked first: if any is wrong, none is set and the error says why. goldilocks-core then re-decides the other parameters, and the result is the new review (as dft_review returns it), shown to the user as a card.

values.description: Setting key to value, e.g. {"task": "phonon"}, {"walltime_h": 24}, {"smearing_type": "cold"}, {"k_grid": [8, 8, 8]} or {"k_grid": null}.

function.name: dft_review
function.description: Preview goldilocks-core's DFT parameter recommendation for the structure and settings currently open in DFT Workbench (must call dft_open_structure first). Read-only, writes no files. Returns each record's value and the source that decided it, the warnings, and `blocking`: decisions goldilocks-core needs before it can generate input files, each with remedies (override patches that resolve it). Ask the user before applying a remedy with dft_set.

function.name: dft_download_bundle
function.description: Generate a real DFT input bundle (e.g. Quantum ESPRESSO input files) for the structure and settings currently open in DFT Workbench (must call dft_open_structure first; it reviews the current settings itself). When goldilocks-core blocks generation, the error names the decisions it needs and their remedies: ask the user instead of calling this again unchanged. No separate confirmation step -- explain what you're about to generate before calling this anyway, since it's a real generation step, but don't ask the user to click a 'confirm' button first. A Download button for the bundle appears right here in the chat -- not on disk directly: tell the user to click it to save the file, browsers don't allow a chat action to save one on its own.

function.name: dft_magnetic_orderings
function.description: List the magnetic orderings goldilocks-core enumerates for the open structure (ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic candidates), as DFT Workbench's Magnetic Orderings card shows them. Only for a spin-polarized calculation. Returns each candidate's label, formula and atom count. The chat doesn't rank them: to compare their energies, tell the user to run mMACE in the card. To use a candidate the user chose, set its label as magnetic_ordering with dft_set.
